title: PortDay
customer: Cruise passengers with a gap of 3 or more hours between their flight and the ship on sailing or landing day in Miami
problem: They're stuck with luggage and nothing to do, often at the terminal or airport, for hours.
solution: A day pass: luggage pick-up at the airport or ship, delivered to the terminal or the flight, plus a short bookable Miami experience in between.
valueProp: Turn dead time into the first (or last) good day of the trip, without dragging bags around.
revenueModel: Per-passenger fee, plus a commission on the experiences booked.
whyNow: PortMiami's record volume: more passengers, and more of them with tight connections.
launchMarketWhy: PortMiami passed 10M cruise passengers in FY2026, above the 8.56M record (PortMiami, Sep. 2026), and one place concentrates the whole customer group.
openQuestions: Will cruise lines let a third party hand luggage over at the terminal?
How many passengers actually have 3+ hours? (source to find)

sources.label: PortMiami, Sep. 2026: Passed 10 million cruise passengers in fiscal year 2026 (Oct. 2025 to Sep. 2026), above the prior record of 8.56 million

author: Ana
